extracted.intended_audience: public company management, securities lawyers, corporate accountants, and SEC reporting teams
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and evaluating public-company non-GAAP financial measures and disclosures to comply with SEC rules (Regulation G and Item 10(e) of Regulation S-K) and recent SEC Division of Corporation Finance interpretive updates. Focuses on labeling, prominence, adjustments, reconciliations, and examples of potentially misleading presentations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulation G: complementary GAAP disclosure and reconciliation
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulation G applies whenever a company discloses a non-GAAP financial measure (including outside of SEC filings) and prohibits such use without complementary disclosure of the most directly comparable GAAP financial measure and a reconciliation of the two measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 100(b) of Regulation G also prohibits the use of materially misleading non-GAAP financial measures. This requirement applies to non-GAAP disclosures outside SEC filings as well as inside filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 10(e) requirements for SEC filings
rubrics_metrics.description: Item 10(e) of Regulation S-K applies to non-GAAP financial measures used in SEC filings and requires the same complementary and reconciling presentation as Regulation G, plus additional requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Item 10(e) requires that the presentation of the most directly comparable GAAP measure be of equal or greater prominence than the corresponding non-GAAP measure, that a statement be included explaining why management believes each non-GAAP financial measure is useful to investors, and a second statement about any additional purposes for which management uses each measure. Item 10(e) also prohibits the use of certain specific non-GAAP financial measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excluding normal, recurring cash operating expenses may be misleading
rubrics_metrics.description: Presenting a performance measure that excludes normal, recurring cash operating expenses necessary to operate a registrant’s business could be considered misleading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Updated guidance clarifies that an operating expense that occurs repeatedly or occasionally, including at irregular intervals, is considered recurring. When evaluating what is a normal operating expense, the staff will consider the nature and effect of the non-GAAP adjustment and how it relates to the company’s operations, revenue generating activities, business strategy, industry and regulatory environment. Companies that exclude cash operating expenses should review the appropriateness of such exclusions in light of this standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individually tailored revenue recognition or measurement adjustments are misleading
rubrics_metrics.description: A non-GAAP measure could be considered misleading under Regulation G if the recognition and measurement principles used to calculate the measure are inconsistent with GAAP; non-GAAP adjustments that change GAAP recognition/measurement principles may be 'individually tailored' and misleading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples the staff may consider misleading include: changing the pattern of recognition (e.g., accelerating revenue recognized ratably under GAAP to when customers are billed); presenting revenue net when GAAP requires gross (or vice versa); and changing the basis of accounting from an accrual basis under GAAP to a cash basis in a non-GAAP measure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate labeling and clear description of non-GAAP measures
rubrics_metrics.description: A non-GAAP measure can be considered misleading if it, and/or any adjustment made to the GAAP measure, is not appropriately labeled and clearly described.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-GAAP measures are not always consistently defined across companies; appropriate labels and clear descriptions of how the non-GAAP measure is calculated are key. Examples of violations include failure to identify and describe a measure as non-GAAP, presenting a non-GAAP measure with a label that does not reflect its nature (e.g., a contribution margin calculated as GAAP revenue less certain expenses labeled 'net revenue'), labeling a non-GAAP measure the same as a GAAP line item or subtotal though calculated differently (e.g., 'Gross Profit' or 'Sales'), or labeling a measure 'pro forma' when it is not calculated consistently with Article 11 of Regulation S-X.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-GAAP measures may be misleading even with detailed disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Even if a non-GAAP measure is accompanied by disclosure about the nature and effect of each adjustment made to the most directly comparable GAAP measure, it can still be considered misleading under Rule 100(b) of Regulation G.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The staff retains discretion to find a particular use of a non-GAAP measure misleading despite extensive, detailed disclosure about adjustments. Detailed disclosure does not guarantee compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal or greater prominence of GAAP measures (prominence requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Item 10(e) requires that when a company discloses a non-GAAP measure it must present the most directly comparable GAAP measure with equal or greater prominence; whether a non-GAAP measure is more prominent depends on facts and circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of undue prominence include: presenting an income statement of non-GAAP measures (i.e., a non-GAAP income statement comprised of non-GAAP measures and including all or most GAAP line items); presenting a non-GAAP measure before the most directly comparable GAAP measure or omitting the comparable GAAP measure altogether (including in earnings release headlines or captions); presenting charts, tables or graphs of non-GAAP financial measures without presenting comparable GAAP charts/tables/graphs with equal or greater prominence; and presenting a ratio where a non-GAAP measure is numerator and/or denominator without also presenting the ratio calculated using the most directly comparable GAAP measure(s) with equal or greater prominence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forward-looking non-GAAP measures: required disclosures when reconciliation unavailable
rubrics_metrics.description: When presenting a forward-looking non-GAAP measure without an accompanying quantitative reconciliation (because reconciliation is not available without unreasonable efforts), certain disclosures are required to avoid the measure being more prominent than the comparable GAAP measure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The company must disclose reliance upon the exemption, identify the information that is unavailable, and disclose the probable significance of that information in a location of equal or greater prominence than the non-GAAP forward-looking measure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconciliations should begin with the most directly comparable GAAP measure
rubrics_metrics.description: The required non-GAAP reconciliation should begin with the comparable GAAP measure (not start with the non-GAAP measure).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Starting the required reconciliation with a non-GAAP measure (as opposed to starting from the comparable GAAP metric) is cited as an example of giving undue prominence to non-GAAP measures and may violate Item 10(e). Companies should ensure reconciliations begin with the GAAP metric.
